findings.description: The 'data' bucket sets no ACL, no bucket policy, and no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, and the in-file comment states the bucket is public. It holds a customer master spreadsheet, so anonymous users could read sensitive customer records.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects such as customer-master.xlsx are stored without enforced server-side encryption or KMS key control.
No logging block is configured, so unauthorized access to this publicly reachable bucket containing customer data would leave no audit trail for detection or forensics.
Versioning is disabled on a publicly exposed bucket, so objects overwritten or deleted by an attacker cannot be recovered, weakening integrity protection and evidence preservation.

A customer master spreadsheet containing apparent PII is uploaded to aws_s3_bucket.data, which is public and unencrypted, and no per-object server_side_encryption or kms_key_id is specified, resulting in direct exposure of sensitive data.
The financials bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, so financial records are stored without configured server-side encryption.
No logging block is configured for a bucket holding financial data, leaving no audit trail of read/write access for forensic or compliance purposes.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with this bucket, so a later ACL or bucket policy change could expose financial data publicly with no guardrail preventing it.
Versioning is not enabled, so accidental or malicious deletion or overwrite of financial records is unrecoverable, and force_destroy is set to true.
The operations bucket defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, so its objects are not covered by enforced server-side encryption.
No logging block is defined, so access to the operations bucket is not recorded for audit or incident response.
No public access block resource restricts this bucket, leaving no defence-in-depth control against a later ACL or policy change exposing it publicly.
The data science bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so datasets are stored without configured encryption at rest, unlike the logs bucket which uses KMS.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is attached, so nothing prevents a subsequent ACL or policy change from exposing the bucket publicly.

The centralized log bucket uses the 'log-delivery-write' canned ACL and has no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block; because it aggregates access logs from other buckets, accidental public exposure would leak access patterns and identities.

findings.issue_category: missing access logging on log bucket
findings.description: The log destination bucket itself has no logging configured, so tampering with or exfiltration of collected audit logs would be untraceable.
